title: Batch-GCD Detection of Larger-Period RSA Primes
summary: Observed repeated RSA prime factors had minimal periods at most 7; whether larger-period primes can occur in only one key, evade batch-GCD detection, and how their periods are distributed remains open.

formal_statement.body: For RSA primes in vulnerable smart-card keys, determine whether primes whose minimal period length exceeds 7 can occur as factors of only one key and therefore evade detection by a batch-GCD computation, and characterize the distribution of such period lengths. Repeated primes observed in the data had minimal period lengths 1, 3, 5, or 7, while tests of length-9, length-11, and length-15 patterns factored four additional keys for length 9 and no new keys for lengths 11 and 15. These observations led to speculation that 3, 5, and 7 are the only factors of the period length, but they do not resolve whether larger-period primes can occur in only one key.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of periodic RSA prime-generation patterns in vulnerable smart-card keys and their detection by batch-GCD computation.
parameters: Minimal period length: measures the repeating pattern associated with a vulnerable RSA prime
Number of keys containing a prime: distinguishes unique factors that evade batch-GCD detection from repeated factors it can detect
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether primes with minimal period length above 7 can occur in only one key and evade batch-GCD detection, and characterize the distribution of such lengths.

citations.label: Factoring RSA Keys from Certified Smart Cards: Coppersmith in the Wild

progress.summary: The source raises the question after observing repeated primes only at minimal period lengths 1, 3, 5, and 7. Length-9 tests factored four more keys, whereas lengths 11 and 15 yielded no new keys, motivating but not resolving the speculation that 3, 5, and 7 are the only factors of the period length.
